title: If air stopped slowing rain, every drop would hit at 1,746 km/h

beats.say: If air stopped slowing rain down, every single drop would hit you at 1,746 kilometres an hour.
beats.speak: If air stopped slowing rain down, every single drop would hit you at one thousand seven hundred and forty six kilometres an hour.

head: REAL RAIN
IS GENTLE.
beats.say: Real rain is gentle. Even the biggest drops, a quarter inch across, land at about 10 metres per second. Your umbrella does fine.
beats.speak: Real rain is gentle. Even the biggest drops, a quarter inch across, land at about ten metres per second. Your umbrella does fine.

head: NOW SWITCH
OFF AIR DRAG.
beats.say: Now switch off air drag, and drop it from the top of a thunderstorm, 12 kilometres up. Nothing slows it down.
beats.speak: Now switch off air drag, and drop it from the top of a thunderstorm, twelve kilometres up. Nothing slows it down.

head: 485 M/S.
FASTER THAN SOUND.
beats.say: It lands at 485 metres per second. 1.41 times the speed of sound. And so does every drop behind it.
beats.speak: It lands at four hundred and eighty five metres per second. One point four one times the speed of sound. And so does every drop behind it.

head: ONE DROP NOW HITS
2,354X HARDER.
beats.say: One 134 milligram drop now carries 15.78 joules. That's 2,354 times the energy of real rain. Your umbrella is gone.
beats.speak: One drop, a hundred and thirty four milligrams, now carries fifteen point seven eight joules. That's two thousand three hundred and fifty four times the energy of real rain. Your umbrella is gone.

head: HEAVY RAIN
ON YOUR ROOF.
beats.say: Heavy rain starts at 7.6 millimetres an hour. On a 100 square metre roof, that's the energy of 21.4 kilograms of TNT, every hour.
beats.speak: Heavy rain starts at seven point six millimetres an hour. On a one hundred square metre roof, that's the energy of twenty one point four kilograms of T N T, every hour.

head: NOW A
HURRICANE.
beats.say: Hurricane Harvey dropped 1 trillion gallons on one Texas county in 4 days. With no air, that rain hits with 106.5 megatons. 7,098 Hiroshimas.
beats.speak: Hurricane Harvey dropped one trillion gallons on one Texas county in four days. With no air, that rain hits with a hundred and six point five megatons. Seven thousand and ninety eight Hiroshimas.

head: SO WHY ARE
YOU STILL DRY?
beats.say: Back to reality. On the way down, air takes 99.96% of every big drop's energy. That's the only reason rain feels like rain.
beats.speak: Back to reality. On the way down, air takes ninety nine point nine six percent of the energy of every big drop. That's the only reason rain feels like rain.

beats.say: Follow Ship With Pip for more.

caption: What if air stopped slowing rain down? Real raindrops top out at about a quarter inch across and land at about 10 m/s (36 km/h). Switch off air drag and drop one from the top of a thunderstorm, 12 km up, and it lands at 485 m/s, or 1,746 km/h: 1.41 times the speed of sound. A 134 mg drop then carries 15.78 joules, 2,354 times the energy of real rain. Heavy rain (7.6 mm an hour) on a 100 square metre roof would hit with the energy of 21.4 kg of TNT every hour. And the 1 trillion gallons Hurricane Harvey dropped on Harris County, Texas in 4 days would hit with 106.5 megatons, 7,098 Hiroshimas. In reality, air takes 99.96% of a big drop's energy on the way down. With no drag, all the energy of the fall turns into speed.
notes: NASA GPM: max terminal speed about 10 m/s for the largest drops. UW-Madison SSEC (wxguys): no raindrop bigger than about a quarter inch; a quarter inch drop falls at about 10 m/s; larger drops break apart. NWS spotter guide: mature thunderstorms often reach 40,000 to 60,000 ft (12 to 18 km); we use the low end, 12 km, as the hypothetical drop height. NOAA JetStream glossary: heavy rain is over 0.30 in/hr (over 7.6 mm/hr). climate.gov (Harris County Flood Control District estimate): one trillion gallons fell in Harris County in four days. OSTI: Hiroshima yield 15 kilotons (15,000 tons of TNT). NIST: g = 9.80665 m/s2 (exact), gallon = 3.785412e-3 m3, ton of TNT = 4.184e9 J (exact), inch = 0.0254 m (exact). Physics Factbook: sound 343 m/s at sea level, 20 C. Constants: water density 1000 kg/m3 (1 litre of water is about 1 kg, used in drop_kg, roof_kg_hr, harvey_kg); roof area 100 m2 is a chosen example size, stated on screen. With no drag, all potential energy m*g*h becomes kinetic, v = sqrt(2gh). The Harvey energy assumes all of that rain fell the full 12 km with no air, a hypothetical. Real rain energy uses the 10 m/s terminal speed of the largest drops.
